questions.stem: Two circles with radii 3 and 5 units have their centers at (2, 3) and (-4, -1), respectively. How many points of intersection do the circles have?
questions.solution: The distance between the centers is sqrt((2-(-4))^2 + (3-(-1))^2) = sqrt(52). Since this distance is less than the sum of their radii (3+5=8), the circles intersect at exactly 2 points.
questions.explanation: To find intersection points, check if center distance < sum of radii. If so, 2 intersections; else, no intersections. Used distance formula: sqrt((x1-x2)^2 + (y1-y2)^2).
questions.common_mistake_notes: Assuming distance ≥ sum of radii means no intersections, but they can touch (1 intersection) if equal.

questions.stem: Circle A has a radius of 7 units and is centered at (5, 2). Circle B has a radius of 4 units and is centered at (-3, -6). How many points of intersection do the circles have?
questions.solution: The distance between centers is sqrt((5-(-3))^2 + (2-(-6))^2) = 8 units. Since this equals the difference of radii (7-4=3), the circles touch at one point, no further intersection.
questions.explanation: If center distance = difference in radii, circles are tangent with 1 intersection point. Used distance formula: sqrt((x1-x2)^2 + (y1-y2)^2).
questions.common_mistake_notes: Assuming sum of radii > distance means no intersections, but they can touch at one point.

questions.stem: Circle C has a radius of 9 units and is centered at (0, 7). Circle D has a radius of 6 units and is centered at (8, -3). How many points of intersection do the circles have?
questions.solution: The distance between centers is sqrt((0-8)^2 + (7-(-3))^2) = 14 units. Greater than sum of radii (9+6=15), no intersection points.
questions.explanation: If center distance > sum of radii, circles do not intersect. Used distance formula: sqrt((x1-x2)^2 + (y1-y2)^2).
questions.common_mistake_notes: Assuming larger radius guarantees intersection; it only means potential intersection.

questions.stem: Circle E has a radius of 4 units and is centered at (-1, -2). Circle F has a radius of 6 units and is centered at (3, 4). How many points of intersection do the circles have?
questions.solution: The distance between centers is sqrt((-1-3)^2 + (-2-4))^2 = 8 units. Less than sum of radii (4+6=10), 2 intersection points.
questions.explanation: If center distance < sum of radii, circles intersect at 2 points. Used distance formula: sqrt((x1-x2)^2 + (y1-y2)^2).
questions.common_mistake_notes: Comparing radii directly is incorrect; consider centers' positions and use distance formula.

questions.stem: Circle G has a radius of 2 units and is centered at (6, 1). Circle H has a radius of 8 units and is centered at (-4, -5). How many points of intersection do the circles have?
questions.solution: The distance between centers is sqrt((6-(-4))^2 + (1-(-5))^2) = 14 units. Less than difference of radii (8-2=6), 2 intersection points.
questions.explanation: If center distance < difference in radii, circles intersect at 2 points. Used distance formula: sqrt((x1-x2)^2 + (y1-y2)^2).
questions.common_mistake_notes: Assuming larger radius means one intersection; it only matters if difference > distance.

questions.stem: Circle I has a radius of 10 units and is centered at (1, -3). Circle J has a radius of 5 units and is centered at (-7, 9). How many points of intersection do the circles have?
questions.solution: The distance between centers is sqrt((1-(-7))^2 + (-3-9))^2 = 14 units. Equal to difference of radii (10-5=5), circles touch at one point, no further intersection.
questions.explanation: If center distance = difference in radii, circles are tangent with 1 intersection point. Used distance formula: sqrt((x1-x2)^2 + (y1-y2)^2).
questions.common_mistake_notes: Assuming larger radius means two intersections; it only matters if difference = distance.

questions.stem: Circle K has a radius of 7 units and is centered at (-2, 5). Circle L has a radius of 3 units and is centered at (4, -1). How many points of intersection do the circles have?
questions.solution: The distance between centers is sqrt((-2-4)^2 + (5-(-1))^2) = 12 units. Greater than sum of radii (7+3=10), no intersection points.
questions.explanation: If center distance > sum of radii, circles do not intersect. Used distance formula: sqrt((x1-x2)^2 + (y1-y2)^2).
questions.common_mistake_notes: Assuming larger radius guarantees intersection; it only means potential intersection.
